comparison: Perfect agreement on motor-related slowing effect (C4, C5, C66, C67, C68, C93). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing that motor tempo is consistently slower than perceptual tempo, with appropriate statistical support. Peer reviewer explicitly describes this as 'valuable for the auditory-motor integration field.'

Perfect agreement on dissociation between overall performance and adaptive flexibility (C81, C82). Both evaluations support the interpretation that aging specifically affects adaptive mechanisms rather than general timing abilities. Peer review implicitly supports this through acceptance of age-related flexibility findings.

Perfect agreement on methodological finding C75. Both evaluations accept this specific result without challenge. OpenEval notes marginal significance and limited robustness; peer review accepts it as consistent with overall experimental design.

Strong agreement on history effects (C6, C7, C51, C52, C53, C69, C70, C71, C72, C73, C74). Both evaluations find comprehensive evidence for historical dependence and hysteresis across perceptual and motor tasks. OpenEval emphasizes replication across experiments; peer reviewers highlight this as a key behavioral feature.

Strong agreement on age-related decline in temporal flexibility (C8, C76, C77, C78). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with appropriate statistical corrections. Peer review additionally references C108 (main conclusion) and notes potential clinical implications. OpenEval notes moderate correlation strength suggesting other contributing factors.

Strong agreement on individual frequency preferences and harmonic relationships (C2, C3, C48, C64, C65). Both evaluations find converging evidence from multiple methodologies convincing. Peer review additionally discusses interpretive claims C79, C80 regarding entrainment framework, which OpenEval evaluates separately in R16.

Agreement on detuning and flexibility relationships (C46, C49, C54, C55). OpenEval finds evidence well-supported with appropriate statistical models. Peer review explicitly affirms detuning evidence and its correlation with flexibility measures, noting it increases credence in entrainment interpretation. Peer review also includes C47, C50 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R7.

Partial overlap on reliability measures. OpenEval focuses on C47, C56, C57, C60 demonstrating measurement reliability across tasks/sessions. Peer review focuses on C56, C57, C60, C61, C62, C63, emphasizing methodological validation and test-retest consistency. Both support the paradigm's utility, though peer review includes additional preference task findings (C61-C63) that OpenEval evaluates separately in R8.

Partial overlap on methodological validation. OpenEval evaluates C61, C62, C63 regarding start-rate condition effects on preference tasks, noting inconsistencies suggesting lower reliability. Peer review groups these with broader reliability findings (C56, C57, C60) and affirms overall experimental design validation without specifically addressing the inconsistencies OpenEval notes.

Partial overlap on theoretical framework. OpenEval evaluates C109, C110 as accurate characterization of timekeeper model predictions supporting entrainment framework argument. Peer review evaluates C107, C109, C110 together, finding the entrainment interpretation accepted but noting it could be strengthened with more explicit contrasts to alternative models (UNCERTAIN evaluation).

Partial overlap on main conclusions. OpenEval evaluates C107, C108 as well-supported summary statements. Peer review evaluates C107, C109, C110 together with UNCERTAIN status, accepting the entrainment interpretation but suggesting it needs stronger contrasts to alternative models.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C107, C108 as main conclusions supported by collective findings. Peer review R4 focuses on age-related findings (C8, C76, C77, C78) and includes C108 as part of affirming the age-related deterioration conclusion.

Minimal overlap on interpretive claims. OpenEval evaluates C79, C80, C93, C94, C95 as plausible interpretations consistent with theoretical frameworks but notes they are inferences not directly tested. Peer review R1 includes C79, C80 alongside empirical findings (C2, C3, C48, C64, C65) and affirms the entrainment interpretation is warranted.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C93 as part of interpretive claims about coupled oscillators. Peer review R2 includes C93 as part of empirical findings on motor-related slowing effect without separately evaluating the theoretical interpretation.
